newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan parties postpone decision on holding firms.
newsitem.headline: Japan parties postpone decision on holding firms.

text.p: Japan's ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) and its allies have postponed a decision to lift a decades-old ban on holding firms from Thursday until Friday, an LDP official said on Wednesday.
The official quoted Taku Yamasaki, chairman of LDP's policy-making committee, as saying that it would be difficult to make a decision by the Thursday deadline.
Yamasaki wanted the three parties -- the LDP, the Social Democratic Party and the small Sakigake party -- to make utmost efforts to reach the agreement on Friday, he said.

One of the reasons for the delay is that the Japan Federation of Employers' Associations (Nikkeiren) and labour unions have not agreed on labour issues which may result from the liberalisation of holding companies, he said.
Jiji news quoted Jiro Nemoto, chairman of Nikkeiren as saying that holding companies are absolutely necessary to revitalise Japan's economy and ensure international competitiveness.
Earlier on Thursday, FTC Secretary-General Shogo Itoda told reporters at a news conference that Japan's anti-monopoly watchdog had expected the three parties to agree on the issue on Thursday.

An agreement between the parties will enable the FTC to work out necessary changes to Japan's anti-monopoly law and submit them to the current session of parliament by March 11, an FTC official said. If submitted by March 11, the legislation could be passed in the current session ending in June and take effect early next year, the official said.
